next: S3 — beads memory. `bd init` on `avo init` (which does not exist yet — introduce it, folding in the .avo/.gitignore + .avo/config.json scaffolding avo commit currently does implicitly, and keep it idempotent per invariant 5). `avo mem add "<insight>"` -> `bd remember`; `avo mem` -> `bd prime`. Each committed version gets a bead linked to its parent via `bd dep add` (readLineage already gives you the parent chain: version N-1 is the parent of N); each FAILED attempt gets an insight bead so the agent stops re-trying dead ends across sessions — decideCommit's refusal path already produces exactly the payload to write (reason, comparison deltas, attempt), so hook it there rather than re-deriving. Graceful degradation is the main design constraint: if `bd` is absent, fall back to lineage/memory.jsonl and warn ONCE (invariant 4) — `bd` is an optional dep in avo doctor and most environments will not have it, so the fallback path is the common path and must be tested first. Verify: avo mem add then avo mem | grep the insight; lineage beads show the correct parent chain via bd show; the no-bd fallback has a test. Note the Runner injection pattern (src/score.ts) is how you unit-test the bd calls without bd installed.

avo mem [--json] lists, `avo mem add "<insight>"` remembers (bd remember with an explicit key so a re-write updates in place), `avo mem prime` is the session-start context (bd prime, or our own digest grouped into insights / dead ends / versions)

avo commit mirrors its own decision into memory: a committed version becomes a bead `<prefix>-v<N>` linked to its parent via `bd dep add`, a refusal becomes an insight bead keyed by content hash so re-attempting the same dead end updates one record instead of piling up. --dry-run / --no-record / a no-op / a harness error write nothing — there is no candidate to learn from
fallback store lineage/memory.jsonl: append-only on write, last-write-wins per key on read, corrupt lines skipped with a warning. It lives in lineage/ so it is a qmd collection like the rest (S4)

src/init.ts: `avo init` — .avo/.gitignore, .avo/config.json, lineage/, optional --scorer <template>, and `bd init --non-interactive --init-if-missing --skip-agents --skip-hooks`. Every step reports created/unchanged/skipped; a second run creates nothing and an edited config is never overwritten (invariant 5). Outside a git repo it refuses and writes nothing. --skip-agents because AGENTS.md belongs to `avo install` (S5); --skip-hooks because a git hook writing during `avo commit` would dirty the tree the commit rule reasons about

fixed a real bug the first run of the new tests caught: avo's own writes must not read as a variation. lineage/memory.jsonl is written AFTER a commit, so with only TRAJECTORY_PATHS filtered the next `avo commit` saw a change the agent never made — it scored an unchanged tree, refused it as no improvement, and remembered that refusal, dirtying the tree again. HARNESS_PATHS (trajectory + .avo/.gitignore + the memory log) now covers the dirtiness check while those files stay staged: they belong in the repo, they are just not evidence of a variation
